# Housekeeping: multiband-compressor

## Authorized scope and smallest closable slice

Review the complete `crates/multiband-compressor` Cargo package and its tests. Deliver practical, behavior-preserving cleanup in this package, or an evidenced no-change verdict when existing choices earn their cost. Cover all five user requests: repeated code/LoC; load-bearing test purposes; avoidable copies; applicable micro SIMD; and data structures that cap efficiency. The user requests two GPT-6.1 Sol xhigh agents concurrently; this overrides the default Terra implementation model for this workflow. Root Sol owns briefing, adversarial review, exact-path checkpoints, integration and remote synchronization.

## Frozen boundaries

Existing public APIs, feature behavior, canonical/wire identities, arithmetic order and per-lane rendered bits, latency/tail, link modes, smoothing and NaN/denormal rules remain contractual. Zero render allocations/frees, locks, I/O or syscalls; no runtime native ISA dispatch. Retain scalar tails, 4-lane Wasm/NEON and x86 AVX2/FMA. Preserve all feature and target configurations. Do not expand another open issue or change DSP algorithms. Read current related issue bodies before touching their subject; discoveries that require architecture or product decisions become bounded follow-ups and final owner questions.

## Implementation and test-value decisions

Prefer deleting or consolidating repetition to adding abstractions that increase total complexity. Assess every existing test or a clearly named homogeneous family by its plausible unique defect; remove trivial, redundant or obsolete cases only after identifying the surviving behavioral gate. Keep independent numeric/oracle, fault, allocation, queue, boundary and target tests. Add/rewrite tests only for a concrete uncovered defect, and state which plausible defect no existing test catches. No prose/source-grep tests, new bit-digest pins or exact resource-byte pins. Copies needed for ownership, snapshots or atomic admission stay unless the same semantics are proved with less work. Data structure changes must preserve deterministic order and bounded realtime work. Inspect applicable hot loops and generated code before claiming additional SIMD; recursive/stateful dependencies alone do not justify changing arithmetic.

## Objective gates and evidence

- Read all production and test files in this package; record concise findings for each of the five requests, concrete changed/deferred locations, and load-bearing test families with retained coverage for deletions.
- Run focused locked package tests and affected feature configurations; use existing downstream/RT/differential gates proportional to the changed contract. Check formatting and package clippy with warnings denied. Relevant Wasm and AArch64 compile checks are required for changed product code; record limitations candidly.
- Changes to DSP arithmetic or hot state need existing independent numeric and scalar/SIMD gates plus one-time base/head evidence when needed; no permanent comparison against the old implementation. Existing research remains the algorithm authority; no new algorithm or listening claim is authorized.
- Benchmarks are optional and descriptive. Any timed measurement freezes its workload/validator, passes zero-workload preflight, and runs exactly one invocation with one warmup/two measured rounds. No timing optimization loop, performance percentage or unsupported sound-quality claim.
- Root conducts one adversarial verdict per coherent attempt, at most five total attempts. Every new/rewritten test gets its unique-defect sentence in that verdict. No-change audits require the same five-axis review, not manufactured edits.
- Stop after a coherent compiling, focused-green tranche; root commits exact owned paths before further edits. Keep edits within `crates/multiband-compressor` and this numbered spec. Independent crates use separate worktrees. Root pushes promptly and updates this GitHub issue with evidence; close only after PASS and evidence upstream, verifying remote state. Merge through the required qualification check and remove clean completed worktrees.

## Sol brief approval and decision record

Approved 2026-10-01 by root Sol within the user's crate-by-crate housekeeping request. Attempt 1 is authorized with the frozen scope/gates above. Owner questions are collected for the final report; routine reversible cleanup proceeds autonomously. Scope is this package's housekeeping, not completion of pre-existing feature/bug issues.

Read all 18 package files, including every source/test/support module, corpus pins and mutation history. **Five axes.** Repetition: skip the first bank member in the loop because its metadata/defaults have already been validated and seeded, preserving all refusals before incompatible/padded fallback. Remove the weaker public width test and its two wrappers; replace the custom unsafe TLS allocator with the already-depended-on audited allocator. Copies: read state sizes directly from the sealed bank program key, continue the rendered donor as the uninterrupted restore reference instead of preparing/rerendering identical prefixes, borrow reset PCM for nonvacuity/filter reference and hoist empty offsets outside the block loop. State staging and independent mutable PCM arms remain necessary. SIMD: the crossover, links, band curves, smoothers and ramp segment loop already use `Lane`; preserve current unfused order, compile-time link/bypass choices, W4/W8 and scalar/tails. No additional simple SIMD transformation earns a claim without changing the frozen graph; source inspection suffices for this preparation/test-only change, with no codegen or speed claim. Structures: fixed arrays for four filter states, two gains, ten ramps, two band caches and twenty pending targets earn deterministic bounded work; preserve them. Net package **−153 lines** (Rust −158, mutation-history notice +5), eight paths, no manifest/lock/G5/arithmetic/API change or benchmark.

### Root adversarial review — attempt 2

Root adversarial verdict: PASS for the frozen housekeeping scope. Root reviewed all implementation/test hunks and the narrow comment-only revision. First-member metadata/defaults are validated before the skipped loop member; every later member is still validated before incompatible/padded fallback. The donor references preserve uninterrupted current state without passing through restore. The shared allocator is actually installed by bench-support, warmed before thread marks, and counts reallocations through allocations. Retention arithmetic, D8, rounded Average products and all original shim tests remain exact; only false/stale documentation is corrected. Debug/release, allocation scopes, numeric/partition and supported-target compile gates satisfy this limited result. Existing #1069/#1073 reproducer exclusions and #893 remain explicit, with no claim that housekeeping fixes them.

Test value: the rewritten allocation/free positive control rejects uninstalled or non-counting own-thread instrumentation; scalar and both-bank-width operation scopes reject render/reset/snapshot/restore heap activity that ordinary PCM/state comparisons cannot see. Continuing the already-rendered donor detects restore/program-transition or full-reset state mistakes against an uninterrupted instance while removing only identical preparation/replay. Borrowed nonvacuity PCM and filter records still catch silent restore/reset or wrong partition-state output; hoisted empty offsets preserve every report/fault assertion. The two renamed split schedules still defend different-track and settled-restatement cache/ramp state, now without false mid-flight claims. The deleted width-only test has the stronger heterogeneous current owner; no new test, generator, historic output pin or DSP expression was introduced.

Revision evidence: focused package formatting/diff checks pass; one-time comparison confirms all non-comment shim lines, including every expression/test, unchanged. No redundant target or numeric workload was rerun.
